newsitem.title: FRANCE: Trichet praises EU budget stability pact - RFTV.
newsitem.headline: Trichet praises EU budget stability pact - RFTV.

text.p: The budgetary stability pact agreed by European Union countries is a good agreement, Bank of France governor Jean-Claude Trichet said on Tuesday.
"I am very happy that the heads of state and government could find a way on agreeing on a good stability pact," Trichet told Reuters Financial Television in an interview.
"I have very great confidence that it is a major element," he said.
EU countries agreed in Dublin last Friday on a pact designed to impose budgetary discipline on EU nations that launch a single currency in 1999.
"The stability pact is of first importance," Trichet said.
"It goes without saying that to run a single currency area you need a good policy mix, and you cannot count only on the credibility of the central bank," he said.
Despite this, the ECB would have great credibility and its independence was a "clear-cut" part of the Maastricht treaty.

"The European Central Bank will have an immense credibility in my opinion because it will have the legacy of the central banks in Europe that have proved themselves and have a very high level of credibility," Trichet said.
"On the other hand you need a good fiscal policy and a good economic policy and this is why the stability pact is so important."
The pact was a milestone for the European Union, he said.

Asked about criticisms of the budget pact made by Bundesbank chief economist Otmar Issing, Trichet said he had not read the comments and noted the pact was agreed by ministers and heads of state of France, Germany and other EU nations.
Issing said in remarks published in the Financial Times on Tuesday that the stability pact did not go far enough to prevent European nations from running up budget deficits.
